newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislators for tax changes for counties.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislators for tax changes for counties.

text.p: California legislators gave final approval late on Saturday to a proposal to change local property tax allocations to benefit the state's cash- strapped local governments.
The legislation was overwhelmingly approved by the Assembly Saturday night. Since it had already been approved by the Senate, the proposal has now advanced to Gov. Pete Wilson.
The legislation would allow California counties, cities and special districts to retain certain funds that would otherwise be shifted to schools and community colleges.

To implement the 1992-1993 and 1993-1994 state budgets, the state Legislature shifted $3.6 billion in property tax revenues from local governments to schools by creating an Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund (ERAF) in each county.

Counties, cities, special districts and redevelopment agencies shift funds to ERAF to reduce the state's funding obligations to school districts and community colleges. County auditors allocate ERAF balances, including the growth in property tax revenues, to these schools and colleges.
Local officials have long objected to their annual property tax shifts, arguing it deprives them of discretionary revenues that could fund development and local programs.

Under the legislation approved Saturday, the growth attributable to ERAF shifts would be retained by counties, cities and special districts. Local governments would retain about $150 million in 1997-1998 under the legislation.

The California State Association of Counties strongly supported the measure. Of the $3.6 billion shifted from local governments to the state in 1992-1993 and 1993-1994, counties lost an estimated $2.6 billion, the association said.
